newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: STATE REVENUE COLLECTION BELOW TARGET.
newsitem.headline: STATE REVENUE COLLECTION BELOW TARGET.

text.p: The head of the Lithuanian parliament's budget and finance committee said on Monday that revenue collection had fallen just short of target for the first four months of the year but the situation was improving.
"At the end of the first quarter we fell short of our target by 86 million litas and on April 25 were still 31 million litas short," Elvyra Kunevichiene said at a news conference.
She said that the gap was narrowed in April when daily collection exceeded the targets by two million litas.

The finance ministry said earlier that the government had collected 1.176 billion litas in the first three months of the year. Kunevichiene said 465 million litas had been collected in in April as of the 25th.
In March, 561 million litas were collected.

Kunevichiene said that the main source for the increase was the recent rise in excise taxes on fuel and alcohol, and improved collection of income tax and the VAT, the main revenue source of the budget.
But she cautioned that the state would still have a tough time meeting its budget commitments.
"Let's have no illusions, though we are improving revenue colection our expenses will be higher in the second quarter of the year," Kunevichiene said.

She said that compensation to people with deposits in banrupt Innovation Bank, payments to the deposit insurance fund, a housing construction fund and a new export encouragement programme would all have to be funded.
"I don't think that we should revise the budget for the second half of the year," Kunevichiene added.
The current Lithuanian government, brought to power in elections last fall, has vowed to improve revenue collection and has declared was on tax evasion, which is rife.
